extracted.intended_audience: community water system operators, state drinking water regulators, certified laboratories, and drinking water compliance personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and approved analytical methods for monitoring drinking water contaminants (including radionuclides, microbiologicals, disinfectant residuals, organics, inorganics) and determining compliance with MCLs under 40 CFR Part 141; includes sampling frequencies, calculation rules, laboratory certification, alternate methods permissions, and tables of approved test methods/editions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iodine-131 quarterly composite sampling
rubrics_metrics.description: For iodine-131, a composite of five consecutive daily samples shall be analyzed once each quarter. As ordered by the State, more frequent monitoring shall be conducted when iodine-131 is identified in the finished water.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strontium-90 and tritium annual monitoring options
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual monitoring for strontium-90 and tritium shall be conducted by means of the analysis of a composite of four consecutive quarterly samples or analysis of four quarterly samples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The latter procedure (analysis of four quarterly samples) is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced monitoring frequency for low gross beta (screening level)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the gross beta particle activity minus the naturally occurring potassium-40 beta particle activity at a sampling point has a running annual average (computed quarterly) less than or equal to 15 pCi/L (screening level), the State may reduce the frequency of monitoring at that sampling point to every 3 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems must collect the same type of samples required in paragraph (b)(2) of this section during the reduced monitoring period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of nuclear facility environmental surveillance data
rubrics_metrics.description: For systems in the vicinity of a nuclear facility, the State may allow the CWS to utilize environmental surveillance data collected by the nuclear facility in lieu of monitoring at the system's entry point(s), where the State determines if such data is applicable to a particular water system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the event of a release from a nuclear facility, systems using surveillance data must begin monitoring at the community water system's entry point(s) in accordance with paragraph (b)(2) of this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: No waiver for State-designated CWS monitoring beta/photon radioactivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Community water systems designated by the State to monitor for beta particle and photon radioactivity can not apply to the State for a waiver from the monitoring frequencies specified in paragraph (b)(1) or (b)(2) of this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potassium-40 subtraction for gross beta screening
rubrics_metrics.description: Community water systems may analyze for naturally occurring potassium-40 beta particle activity from the same or equivalent sample used for the gross beta particle activity analysis and are allowed to subtract the potassium-40 beta particle activity value from the total gross beta particle activity value to determine if the screening level is exceeded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The potassium-40 beta particle activity must be calculated by multiplying elemental potassium concentrations (in mg/L) by a factor of 0.82.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action when gross beta minus K-40 exceeds screening level
rubrics_metrics.description: If the gross beta particle activity minus the naturally occurring potassium-40 beta particle activity exceeds the appropriate screening level, an analysis of the sample must be performed to identify the major radioactive constituents present in the sample and the appropriate doses must be calculated and summed to determine compliance with § 141.66(d)(1), using the formula in § 141.66(d)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doses must also be calculated and combined for measured levels of tritium and strontium to determine compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly monitoring after MCL exceedance and return-to-frequency rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must monitor monthly at the sampling point(s) which exceed the maximum contaminant level in § 141.66(d) beginning the month after the exceedance occurs and must continue monthly monitoring until the system has established, by a rolling average of 3 monthly samples, that the MCL is being met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems who establish that the MCL is being met must return to quarterly monitoring until they meet the requirements set forth in paragraph (b)(1)(i) or (b)(2)(iv) of this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: State discretion to require more frequent monitoring or confirmation samples
rubrics_metrics.description: The State may require more frequent monitoring than specified in paragraphs (a) and (b) of this section, or may require confirmation samples at its discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The results of the initial and confirmation samples will be averaged for use in compliance determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring timing designated by State
rubrics_metrics.description: Each public water systems shall monitor at the time designated by the State during each compliance period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance determined at each sampling point
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with § 141.66 (b) through (e) will be determined based on the analytical result(s) obtained at each sampling point. If one sampling point is in violation of an MCL, the system is in violation of the MCL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Running annual average for systems monitoring > once per year
rubrics_metrics.description: For systems monitoring more than once per year, compliance with the MCL is determined by a running annual average at each sampling point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the average of any sampling point is greater than the MCL, then the system is out of compliance with the MCL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate noncompliance if any sample causes running average to exceed MCL
rubrics_metrics.description: For systems monitoring more than once per year, if any sample result will cause the running average to exceed the MCL at any sample point, the system is out of compliance with the MCL immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include all samples in compliance determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must include all samples taken and analyzed under the provisions of this section in determining compliance, even if that number is greater than the minimum required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance when required samples not all collected
rubrics_metrics.description: If a system does not collect all required samples when compliance is based on a running annual average of quarterly samples, compliance will be based on the running average of the samples collected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of non-detects in annual averages
rubrics_metrics.description: If a sample result is less than the detection limit, zero will be used to calculate the annual average, unless a gross alpha particle activity is being used in lieu of radium-226 and/or uranium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the gross alpha particle activity result is less than detection, 1/2 the detection limit will be used to calculate the annual average.

rubrics_metrics.name: State discretion to delete obvious sampling/analytic errors
rubrics_metrics.description: States have the discretion to delete results of obvious sampling or analytic errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirements for radioactivity MCL exceedance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the MCL for radioactivity set forth in § 141.66 (b) through (e) is exceeded, the operator of a community water system must give notice to the State pursuant to § 141.31 and to the public as required by subpart Q of this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate analytical techniques permission and equivalency
rubrics_metrics.description: With the written permission of the State, concurred in by the Administrator of the U.S. EPA, an alternate analytical technique may be employed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An alternate technique shall be accepted only if it is substantially equivalent to the prescribed test in both precision and accuracy as it relates to the determination of compliance with any MCL. The use of the alternate analytical technique shall not decrease the frequency of monitoring required by this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified laboratory requirement for compliance determination
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purpose of determining compliance with §§ 141.21 through 141.27, 141.40, 141.74, 141.89, 141.402, 141.901, and 141.902, samples may be considered only if they have been analyzed by a laboratory certified by EPA or the State
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except that measurements of alkalinity, disinfectant residual, orthophosphate, pH, silica, temperature, and turbidity may be performed by any person acceptable to the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: State may take samples or use State-taken samples to determine compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this part shall be construed to preclude the State or any duly designated representative of the State from taking samples or from using the results from such samples to determine compliance by a supplier of water with the applicable requirements of this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring modification for consecutive public water systems
rubrics_metrics.description: When a public water system supplies water to one or more other public water systems, the State may modify the monitoring requirements imposed by this part to the extent that the interconnection of the systems justifies treating them as a single system for monitoring purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any modified monitoring shall be conducted pursuant to a schedule specified by the State and concurred in by the Administrator of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix A: only specified editions of methods are approved
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the editions stated in the following table are approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative testing methods listed in Appendix A are limited to the specific edition/version entries shown in the tables; other editions are not approved unless listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved alternative methods for total coliforms (40 CFR 141.21(f)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative Testing Methods for Contaminants Listed at 40 CFR 141.21(f)(3) — Total Coliforms: approved methodologies include Total Coliform Fermentation Technique (SM 21st/22nd/SM Online etc., methods 9221 A,B), Total Coliform Membrane Filter Technique (9222 A,B,C), Presence-Absence (P-A) Coliform Test (9221 D), ONPG-MUG Test (9223 / 9223 B), Colitag™/Modified Colitag™, Tecta EC/TC, and others as listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the editions/versions and method numbers listed in the table may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved alternative methods for fecal coliforms (40 CFR 141.21(f)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative Testing Methods for Contaminants Listed at 40 CFR 141.21(f)(5) — Fecal Coliforms: Fecal Coliform Procedure (method 9221 E / 9221 E-06) and equivalents as listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved alternative methods for E. coli (40 CFR 141.21(f)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative Testing Methods for Contaminants Listed at 40 CFR 141.21(f)(6) — E.coli: ONPG-MUG Test (9223 B series), Colitag™/Modified Colitag™, Tecta EC/TC, and other listed methods (incl. SM editions and SM Online references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved methods for inorganics and trace elements (40 CFR 141.23(k)(1) table)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix A lists approved methodologies and method numbers/editions for many inorganic and trace element contaminants (e.g., alkalinity titrimetric 2320 B; antimony hydride-AA D 3697; arsenic atomic absorption/furnace 3113 B; ICP-AES EPA 200.5 Rev 4.2; barium ICP 3120 B or AA 3111 D; etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each contaminant's approved methods are the specific EPA/SM/ASTM or 'Other' entries shown in the table and only the listed editions/method numbers are approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved methods for volatile organic compounds and semivolatiles (40 CFR 141.24(e)(1) and 141.131 etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative Testing Methods for Contaminants Listed at 40 CFR 141.24(e)(1) and related sections list approved methods such as Purge & Trap/GC/MS (EPA 524.3, 524.4) for benzene and many VOCs; GC/ECD for certain pesticides; SPE/GC/MS (525.3) for many semivolatiles; and specific method numbers/editions are specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only the EPA method numbers and editions (and listed SM/ASTM/Other methods) shown in the tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved methods for naturally occurring and man-made radionuclides (40 CFR 141.25(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative Testing Methods for Contaminants Listed at 40 CFR 141.25(a) specify approved methodologies and method numbers for gross alpha/beta, radium-226, radium-228, uranium, radioactive cesium, radioactive iodine, strontium 89/90, tritium, and gamma emitters (e.g., evaporation 900.0 Rev 1.0; liquid scintillation 7110 D; radon emanation 903.1; radiochemical methods 903.0/904.0; ICP-MS 3125 for uranium; radiochemical 7500-Sr B for strontium; etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the listed method numbers/editions may be used for compliance monitoring of the specified radionuclides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved methods for total coliform, heterotrophic bacteria, turbidity, and related (40 CFR 141.74(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative Testing Methods for Contaminants Listed at 40 CFR 141.74(a)(1) include Total Coliform Fermentation Technique (9221 A,B,C), Total Coliform Membrane Filter Technique (9222 A,B,C), ONPG-MUG Test (9223/9223 B), heterotrophic bacteria pour plate method (9215 B), and turbidity nephelometric methods (2130 B) including on-line and portable laser/LED nephelometry with listed device/method approvals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific instrument/method approvals (e.g., Hach Method numbers, Mitchell methods, Lovibond devices) are enumerated and only the listed versions are approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved methods for disinfectant residuals (40 CFR 141.74(a)(2) and 141.131(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative Testing Methods for Disinfectant Residuals list approved methodologies and method numbers for free chlorine, total chlorine, chlorine dioxide, ozone, etc., including amperometric titration (4500-Cl D), DPD colorimetric (4500-Cl G), amperometric sensors, on-line chlorine analyzers (EPA 334.0), and device-specific approvals (ChloroSense, ChlordioX Plus), with SM/ASTM references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the enumerated methods and device-method revisions in the table are approved; some on-line or sensor methods have specific listed approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-approved test strips as approved alternative for free chlorine (40 CFR 141.131(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: If Approved by the State: Free Chlorine — Test Strips Method D99-003 (Method D99-003, Revision 3.0) may be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State approval is required; the specific test strip method/version indicated is the approved method if concurred by the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved methods for TOC, DOC, UV254, SUVA (40 CFR 141.131(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Parameter methodologies in Appendix A for Total Organic Carbon (TOC), Dissolved Organic Carbon (DOC), UV254, and Specific UV Absorbance (SUVA) include High Temperature Combustion (5310 B), Persulfate-UV or Heated Persulfate Oxidation (5310 C), wet oxidation (5310 D), and EPA method 415.3 revisions for TOC/DOC/UV methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the listed SM and EPA methods/editions are approved for monitoring these parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods with MRL ≤ 0.0010 mg/L for bromate monitoring (40 CFR 141.132(b)(3)(ii)(B))
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative Testing Methods With MRL ≤0.0010 mg/L for Monitoring Listed at 40 CFR 141.132(b)(3)(ii)(B): Bromate — Two-Dimensional Ion Chromatography (IC) 302.0 and IC-ESI-MS/MS (EPA method 557) are listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods meeting the stated MRL requirement are the only acceptable low-level methods specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved E. coli methods for various parts (e.g., 141.402(c)(2), 141.704, 141.852)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix A lists multiple approved E. coli detection methods across different parts (Colilert 9223 B series, Colisure, Colilert-18, Readycult, Colitag, Chromocult, EC-MUG, NA-MUG, mColiBlue24, Tecta EC/TC, RAPID'E.coli 2, and others) along with method numbers and approved editions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only the specific method versions/editions listed for the relevant CFR part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved method for Cryptosporidium (40 CFR 141.704(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Cryptosporidium — Filtration/Immunomagnetic Separation/Immunofluorescence Assay Microscopy (EPA Method 1623.1) is the approved method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix lists EPA Method 1623.1 (2012) as the approved methodology for Cryptosporidium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved E. coli membrane filtration two-step for 141.704(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: E. coli — Membrane Filtration, Two Step (9222 D/9222 G) is listed as an approved alternative testing method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved methods for TTHM, HAA5, bromate and related (40 CFR 141.131(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative Testing Methods for Contaminants Listed at 40 CFR 141.131(b)(1) include P&T/GC/MS (524.3, 524.4) for TTHM, LLE/GC/ECD or IC-ESI-MS/MS for HAA5 (6251 B series, EPA 557), Two-Dimensional IC for bromate (302.0), and other listed methods for haloacetic acids and disinfection byproducts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only those EPA/SM/Other method numbers and editions listed may be used for compliance monitoring of these DBPs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved methods for disinfectant residuals (parameter-specific entries and on-line/analyzer approvals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix contains repeated entries across parts for approved disinfectant residual methods (e.g., amperometric titration, DPD colorimetric, amperometric sensors, on-line analyzers EPA 334.0) with specific method numbers and device-method approvals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Device-specific method approvals (e.g., ChloroSense, ChlordioX Plus) are enumerated and only listed revisions/versions are approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix cross-reference requirement: use only listed SM/ASTM/EPA/Other editions
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout Appendix A the tables repeatedly indicate that only the specified Standard Methods (SM editions), EPA methods, ASTM methods, and 'Other' named methods (with revisions and method numbers) are approved for use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The footnotes list the sources/availability for specific methods and reinforce that only the enumerated versions in the tables are approvable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved methods for a wide range of organic pesticides and herbicides (specific entries)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix enumerates approved methods for specific pesticides/herbicides (e.g., atrazine LC/ESI-MS/MS EPA 536; alachlor SPE/GC/MS 525.3; simazine LC/ESI-MS/MS 536 or 525.3/523; glyphosate HPLC with derivatization 6651 B; and many others).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each named contaminant must be analyzed only by the specified approved methodology and method number/edition listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved methods for metals and elements in 40 CFR 143.4(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative Testing Methods for Contaminants Listed at 40 CFR 143.4(b) include approved methods for aluminum, chloride, color, foaming agents, iron, manganese, silver, sulfate, TDS, zinc, etc., listing AVICP-AES EPA 200.5 Rev 4.2, atomic absorption methods (3111/3113), ICP (3120 B), ion chromatography, gravimetric, titrimetric, and method-specific references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the listed methods and editions may be used for compliance monitoring under 40 CFR 143.4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Device- or vendor-specific method approvals and citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix A includes approvals for vendor/device-specific methods (e.g., Hach Method numbers, Mitchell methods, Lovibond devices, AMI Turbiwell, ChloroSense, ChlordioX Plus, Thermo Fisher discrete analyzer) with specific revision dates and citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These device-specific methods are approvable only in the listed versions/revisions and should be procured/used consistent with the indicated documentation sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnote and source citations constrain method availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnotes and references at the end of Appendix A (numbered references to Standard Methods editions, EPA method documents, ASTM, device manufacturers, and availability URLs) indicate where approved method documents are available and reiterate that only the listed versions are approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users must consult the cited primary method documents (SM, EPA, ASTM, vendor docs) for method details and ensure the exact edition/revision listed is followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: State concurrence requirement where specified
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple provisions (e.g., alternate analytical techniques, modified monitoring schedules for consecutive systems, device/test strip acceptance) require written permission or concurrence by the State and, in some cases, concurrence by the Administrator of the U.S. EPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain and document the required State (and EPA Administrator where stated) concurrence/permission before relying on alternate methods, modified monitoring, or substituted data sources.
